sections.h2: Where to take a deed for recording
sections.html:
The Morgan County Recorder's Office is in the Riecker Building at 155 East Main Street, Room 160, McConnelsville, OH 43756. Call 740-962-4051, or email recorder@morgancountyohio.gov. More is on the county recorder page.

The Auditor works from the same building and answers at 740-962-4475. Even so, a Morgan County deed does not go straight to the Recorder. Questions about prior deeds and recording fees go to the Recorder's counter on the first floor, so call that number before you drive in.

sections.h2: The order of offices for a deed
sections.html:
A deed starts at the County Engineer, moves to the Auditor and ends at the Recorder. The same route applies to transfer on death designations, land contracts, easements and covenants, and Auditor staff will take your papers to the other offices in the proper order. The details are in the Auditor's real estate FAQ.

The Engineer's number is 740-962-3171. The county's conveyance standards want these items in or attached to any document that transfers land:

  • The parcel number.
  • A full legal description.
  • The property address.
  • A reference to the prior instrument.
  • The tax-mailing address.

Signatures must be legible, and a printed name below an unclear signature is accepted. After the Auditor finishes, the county's property website refreshes within one to two business days.

sections.h2: What the Auditor collects on a sale
sections.html:
The Auditor's transfer page lists the charges that come before recording. The office takes cash, or a check made out to the Morgan County Auditor.

Morgan County Auditor transfer charges
ChargeAmount
Conveyance fee$3.00 per $1,000 (sale price x .003)
Transfer fee$0.50 per parcel
Split fee, for every split$100.00

State law sets the floor for the Auditor's fee in section 319.54, at $1 or ten cents on each $100. Section 322.02 lets commissioners add a local transfer tax with a ceiling of 30 cents per $100. If your closing statement needs a separate line for each, ask the Auditor how the $3.00 figure divides. For acreage splits, call the Engineer, since the survey and the split fee start there.

Call 740-962-4051 and ask for the current fee sheet. The ceiling comes from section 317.32. Two pages carry $17 for the recorder and $17 for the housing trust fund, and each page beyond them adds $4 and $4. On top, the county may tack on a preservation surcharge, capped at $5 an instrument.

The same section prices a certified copy at $1 plus $1 per page, a counter photocopy likewise, and a marginal reference made by separate instrument at $2 plus $2. Page counts use legal-size sheets and include the caption page, which is why a third page raises the bill.

sections.h2: Is a transfer taxable if no money changes hands?
sections.html:
It can be. A sale is taxable, and so is a gift with no money involved unless an exemption fits. Only the relationships listed on the DTE 100EX form are exempt, and the filer reads each lettered choice to see whether one fits.

The statute lists many of those exemptions in section 319.54(G)(3), including transfers among heirs of one decedent when no money is paid and transfers to the grantor of a trust the grantor can revoke. If someone on the deed has died, families are pointed to Morgan County Probate Court at 740-962-2861 when there is a will, and to a title agent or real estate lawyer when a survivorship deed or transfer on death designation was recorded.

Section 319.202 (full text) also has the buyer certify what the seller said about reduced taxes and farm-use valuation. An owner who sells a home that carried the homestead reduction also files form DTE 101, the Statement of Conveyance of Homestead Property. The farm program (CAUV) carries a $25 one-time filing fee and requires crops, animals or timber on at least 10 acres.

sections.h2: Parcels and tax bills after a sale
sections.html:
Parcel changes take effect at once, but the bills lag. After combining parcels, the owner keeps getting separate paper bills until the next tax year, and the owner of an original parcel receives the tax bill for the whole original parcel until the next year after a split. Raise that with a title company or real estate attorney before the sale closes.

Taxes are due in February and July, and the Treasurer at 740-962-3561 bills and collects them. Value complaints go to the Auditor between New Year's Day and the end of March. The standard Homestead Exemption exempts $25,000 of a home's market value for qualifying seniors and for owners who are permanently and totally disabled, with a $50,000 enhanced version for a qualifying disabled veteran.

sections.h2: Why a property's value can change
sections.html:
Value changes come from a short list of causes:

  • A full reappraisal, which Ohio law requires of every parcel once every six years.
  • A countywide update in the third year of that cycle, based on market trends.
  • New construction, as shown by local permits.
  • Corrections to square footage, bedroom or bathroom counts.
  • A Board of Revision decision, or damage to or destruction of the property.

The Board of Revision has three members: the Auditor, the Treasurer and the president of the county commissioners, or their designees. It adjusts values, not tax dollars. Ohio law generally allows one filing in a three-year period, and withdrawing a complaint still counts as that filing. Corporations should have an attorney file for them.

If you think your value is too high before you list, compare the parcel record with the house itself. Square footage, bedroom and bathroom counts are the easiest errors to fix, and a correction needs no hearing.

Plan the order of the offices when you set a closing date. Because Auditor staff carry papers between counters, leave a few business days between signing and the date you need the deed recorded, and ask the Recorder's counter what it needs on the first floor.

The 2025 estimate is 13,626 residents, down 1.3% from the 2020 base, with 7,437 housing units. Nearly four homes in five (78.9%) are owner-occupied. Median home value is $150,900 and median household income is $59,351. Only 23 building permits were issued in 2025.

With about 33 people per square mile, many sales involve acreage. The Engineer's survey and split steps are worth planning for if you are selling part of a larger tract. A cash buyer shortens the closing but not the Engineer, Auditor and Recorder sequence.

faqs.q: Where is the Morgan County Recorder located?
faqs.a: It is in the Riecker Building, 155 East Main Street, Room 160, McConnelsville, OH 43756. The phone is 740-962-4051.

faqs.q: Who do I see first when I sell land in Morgan County?
faqs.a: Start with the County Engineer at 740-962-3171, then the Auditor, then the Recorder. The Auditor's staff will deliver your documents to the other offices in order.

faqs.q: What is the conveyance fee in Morgan County?
faqs.a: The Auditor charges $3.00 per $1,000 of sale price, plus a $0.50 per parcel transfer fee and a $100.00 split fee for every split. Payment is by cash or a check to the Morgan County Auditor.

faqs.q: Is a gift of a house taxable in Morgan County?
faqs.a: It can be. Only the relationships listed on the DTE 100EX exemption form qualify as exempt, so read each choice on that form or ask the Auditor at 740-962-4475.

faqs.q: How much will Morgan County charge to record my deed?
faqs.a: Call the Recorder at 740-962-4051 and ask for the current fee sheet. The state schedule behind it is $34 for two pages, $8 for each more, and a county may add up to $5 per instrument for preservation.
